general_information.Description: This course covers crisis communication theory, crisis management approaches, classic cases and the influence of culture on crisis communication. This course will introduce the definitions of crisis and how they come about, the importance of the Enterprise Risk Management framework in crisis prevention and preparation, and how we can recognise and address crises in case they happen. This course focuses on the role of communications throughout the crisis management process, as well as how to utilise media relations and social media to prevent and/or respond to crises. Apart from learning academic theories, students will have opportunities to apply their acquired knowledge & skills in analysing a real-world case study, as well as developing a industry-facing crisis communication plan for an organisation ("client") and self-organising an accompanied simulated media conference to address a crisis of that organisation. Throughout that, students will be equipped with practical experience and skills to be ready for their future career path in the communications field. Finally, students can also use AI to assist their practices and assignemnts.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by instructor after class - Use their own laptop in class only for learning purpose - Read the textbook in advance - Access the course websites (https://flm.fpt.edu.vn) for up-to-date information and material of the course.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify organisational, industrial and environmental challenges and disasters
Demonstrate an understanding of the concepts, theories and practice of issues management and crisis communication.
Utilize AI to analyse and develop strategies for organisational issues using the theories, models and methods of issues management and crisis communication
Gain the capacity to critique organisational and industrial responses to issues and crises in terms of attitude and ethics
Develop a critical attitude towards crisis communications management
Identify and apply ethical standards of practice when dealing with issues management and crisis communication
Skills in analysis and problem solving; AI Literacy and Responsible Communication; Proficient in presentation and teamwork skills; positive contributing attitude in the class and groupworks

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the acquainted knowledge which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 1, 6, 7, 8)
assessments.Grading Guide: Individual Assessment (At home) Type: Essay Weight: 15% Length: 1,500-2,000 words Task Description: Choose from the list of crisis case studies provided by the lecturer before and analyse one organisational crisis. Your essay will include an overview of the crisis, a description of the organisation, a crisis timeline, actions and responses taken, a media analysis, stakeholder impacts, lessons learned, recommendations, and use appropriate matrix/models. The essay should address the criteria as outlined in the assessment task and rubric mentioned during the class. Students should use a mix of scholarly references, media coverage and organisational materials, as well as applying AI-tools to collect information and analyze the chosen crisis.

assessments.CLO: CLO1, CLO2, CLO3, CLO4, CLO5, CLO6, CLO7
assessments.Question Type: The whole class is divided into groups. Each group is assigned to make one crisis communication plan
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the acquainted knowledge and skills which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 1-8, with an emphasis on Chapter 2-5)
assessments.Grading Guide: Group Assessment Type: Crisis Communication Plan (At Home) + Presentation (In the class) Weight: 25% Task Description: Students working within a small group setting of 4-6 students to select one organisation in Vietnam, which must be accepted by the lecturer, then propose a crisis communication plan for that organisation. The plan must showcase all knowledge the students have gained in the class, and be delivered as a final report to their chosen organisation. AI Application: Students have to demonstrate their capability of applying AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, etc...) in preparing templates in the crisis communication plan, which include (but aren't limited to) prewritten news release(s) and media alert. Presentation: For the 15-minute presentation, each group have to showcase all of your key points mentioned in your report in front of your classmates. Notes: The detailed structure of a crisis communication plan could be found in the textbook (Chapter 5) Further details of the crisis communication plan will be provided in class. The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.
assessments.Note: The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

assessments.Question Type: The whole class is divided into groups. Each group is assigned to create one simulated media conference.
assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the acquainted knowledge and skills which student obtained in the delivered chapters (Chapter 4-7)
assessments.Grading Guide: Group Assessment Type: Simulated Media Conference (In the class) Weight: 20% Based on your crisis communication plan, each group will prepare for a media conference based on the scenario which will respond to a simulated crisis of your chosen organisation. Your media statement should be no more than 15 minutes in total and will be followed by a 15-minute Q&A from the “journalist” members of the class. Before the media conference, your group have to prepare: 1. a media alert 2. a media kit, including the press release (to be delivered at the conference) 3. a one-page summary of key message AI Application: Students have to demonstrate their capability of applying AI tool (ChatGPT, Claude.ai, etc...) in preparing the above-mentioned documents. Notes: Further details of the media conference will be provided in class. The detailed marking criteria for this assessment will be provided to you by your lecturer.
assessments.Note: The mark will be given based on each student's performance, not on the whole group's. It means each student will get their own mark.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: The questions will cover the lectures, class discussions, activities, exercises, and textbook.
